intro.title: Feature Flag Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useFeatureFlag` that allows you to dynamically enable or disable parts of your application's UI based on a configuration. You'll learn the core concept of custom hooks, which let you extract and reuse stateful logic across components. The main technologies involved are React hooks (specifically `useState` and `useEffect`) and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that can check feature flags and control what users see in your app.
intro.usecase: Feature flags are used in production applications to control feature rollouts, perform A/B testing, and enable emergency kill switches. For example, e-commerce platforms use feature flags to gradually release new checkout flows to subsets of users, while dashboard applications use them to toggle between old and new analytics panels. As a developer, you'll implement feature flag hooks to conditionally render UI components like promotional banners, experimental settings panels, or beta features in user profiles. This pattern allows teams to deploy code safely without exposing unfinished features to all users simultaneously.
